methodological_rigor.justification: This is a large multicentre ENSAT retrospective cohort from 14 reference centres (2000-2022, follow-up to October 2024) comprising 1315 ACC patients including the largest ever cohorts of rare subtypes (179 oncocytic, 28 myxoid, 10 sarcomatoid). Strengths include Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, univariate and multivariate Cox regression, and 1:3 propensity score matching on sex, age, and ENSAT stage. Adrenal expert pathology review in most centres. Limitations explicitly acknowledged: retrospective referral/selection bias, Ki67 could not be included in propensity matching due to missing data, heterogeneous treatment and follow-up protocols, single-centre origin of the conventional ACC control group (Würzburg), and underpowering of myxoid/sarcomatoid analyses. Conservative framing of myxoid/sarcomatoid conclusions as exploratory is appropriate.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual longitudinal/retrospective cohort with national and international scope, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: the finding that stage-adjusted oncocytic ACC has significantly longer RFS (HR 0.41) and OS (HR 0.35) compared to conventional ACC provides prognostic guidance, and the finding that mitotane monotherapy and platinum-based chemotherapy efficacy in oncocytic ACC is comparable to conventional ACC directly informs treatment decisions. The conclusion that oncocytic histology alone should not change surveillance or adjuvant treatment strategy is clinically actionable.

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational cohort, STROBE applies. The manuscript reports study design, setting (14 centres), eligibility criteria, outcome definitions (RFS from R0 resection, OS from diagnosis), statistical methods (Fisher, Wilcoxon, Cox, propensity score matching), ethical approval and informed consent, inclusion/exclusion (15 patients with local pathologist-only diagnosis), and missing data limitations. ENSAT registry and RedCap data collection are described. The manuscript notes an insertion about a CONSORT diagram in supplementary material but this reads as an editorial artifact. Data availability is not described (referenced supplementary tables only); no repository or sharing plan is stated. Reporting of HRs with 95% CIs and P values is thorough.

novelty_literature.justification: This is by far the largest cohort of rare ACC subtypes ever assembled, with 179 oncocytic, 28 myxoid, and 10 sarcomatoid ACCs compared against 1098 conventional ACCs. Prior literature included only a cumulative 66 oncocytic patients across multiple studies with conflicting results; this study resolves that discrepancy with rigorous propensity score matching. The treatment-efficacy comparison for oncocytic ACC with mitotane and EDP-M is also novel. Myxoid/sarcomatoid analyses, though exploratory, are among the first comparative survival analyses for these ultra-rare variants.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-structured with clear abstract, methods, and results, with detailed Tables 1-3 reporting baseline characteristics, RFS prognostic factors, and propensity-matched outcomes. Figures 1-2 present Kaplan-Meier curves. The discussion is comprehensive and explicitly addresses prior conflicting studies (Renaudin, Mills, Prinzi, Shirali). One awkward editorial remnant ('After this part an additional sentence should be included...') indicates incomplete copy-editing. Otherwise writing is clear with appropriate caution for underpowered subgroups.

key_strengths: Largest ever cohort of rare ACC subtypes (179 oncocytic, 28 myxoid, 10 sarcomatoid) against 1098 conventional ACCs across 14 ENSAT reference centres
Rigorous dual analytic approach combining multivariate Cox regression with 1:3 propensity score matching on sex, age, and ENSAT stage
Clinically actionable finding that stage-adjusted oncocytic ACC has favourable RFS (HR 0.41) and OS (HR 0.35) but similar mitotane/EDP-M efficacy, informing surveillance and treatment decisions
Resolves prior conflicting literature (Shirali vs Renaudin/Prinzi) with a large, well-matched cohort
Appropriately conservative framing of underpowered myxoid/sarcomatoid analyses as exploratory
key_concerns: Ki67 index could not be included in propensity score matching due to missing data, leaving an unadjusted prognostic factor
Conventional ACC control cohort sourced from a single centre (Würzburg), potentially introducing referral bias
Retrospective design with heterogeneous treatment and follow-up protocols across centres
Myxoid (n=28) and sarcomatoid (n=10) subgroups are statistically underpowered for definitive conclusions
Editorial artefact ('After this part an additional sentence should be included...') indicates incomplete copy-editing
No explicit data availability or sharing plan
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed, clinically informative multicentre registry study resolving a prognostic question in a rare cancer with the largest cohort to date; appropriate for Tier 2 with minor revisions including copy-editing and Ki67-adjusted sensitivity analyses.
